why: codex prints this on EVERY run, including with stdin on /dev/null where it reads EOF and continues normally. M0 recorded it as the signal of an imminent hang; rechecked against the real binary, it is not. Treating it as a protocol error failed every codex run before it produced a single event, and `codex exec --help` confirms stdin is simply an additional input channel. A hang is only detectable by a timeout, which belongs to the host

why: stderr is diagnostics. Unlike stdout, an unrecognised line here is NOT promoted to unknown — engines print progress chatter to stderr, and an event per line would bury the transcript
